subject: sentences
title: Little stories
about: One-sentence stories in Unit 1 and 2 words followed by a who, what, where, why, how-many or feeling question. This is the first step of reading for meaning, not just sounding out.
tip: If he is stuck, have him read the story sentence again out loud before looking at the choices.

cards.q: Sam has a red hat. What color is Sam's hat?
cards.note: The answer is right there in the story.

cards.q: The cat naps on the bed. Where is the cat?
Pam ran to the bus. Who ran to the bus?
The dog dug in the mud. What did the dog do?
cards.note: What did it do asks about an action.

cards.q: Tim has six cups on a shelf. How many cups does Tim have?
cards.note: How many asks for a number.

cards.q: The duck swims in the pond. Where is the duck?
Meg fed the hen. Who fed the hen?
The frog sat on a log. What did the frog sit on?
cards.note: Find the word after sat on.

cards.q: Ben fell in the pond and got wet. Why is Ben wet?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The story tells us what happened first.

cards.q: The big dog is sad. How does the dog feel?
cards.note: How does it feel asks about a feeling.

cards.q: The hen sits on the eggs. What does the hen sit on?
cards.note: Find the words after sits on. Hens really do sit on their eggs to keep them warm.

cards.q: Kim can hop and skip. What can Kim do?
cards.note: Both words come from the story.

cards.q: The red fox hid in the den. Where did the fox hide?
Max lost his cap. What did Max lose?
